chokepointR: Global Trade Chokepoint Risks and Resilience

Source: R/chokepointR-package.R
chokepointR-package.Rd

Profiles the disruption risk and resilience of the world's major maritime trade chokepoints – the eight straits and canals through which a large share of seaborne trade and oil must pass. For each chokepoint it combines how much world trade depends on it, route substitutability, a panel of graph-theory centrality indicators (weighted and unweighted betweenness, degree and weighted strength, harmonic centrality and PageRank) computed on the country-chokepoint trade-dependency network, quantitative traffic and cargo context (vessel transits, vessel and cargo mix, trade shares, local economic dependence), documented disruption incidents (2018 onward, each with a resolvable citation), and composite resilience and vulnerability indices, to support assessment of how exposed supply chains and global value chains are to trade-route disruption. Every quantitative figure carries a per-cell source, URL and confidence flag. Trade-dependency, systemic-risk and centrality measures build on Verschuur and Hall (2025) doi:10.5281/zenodo.13841881 ; oil-transit figures are from the U.S. Energy Information Administration. An optional helper queries a live hazard feed (USGS) without redistributing third-party data.
